endorsements.quote: Low-risk workflow tools (e.g. documentation support or dashboards) differ fundamentally from clinical decision-support systems and should follow appropriate validation pathways, including model registries, institutional approval processes, and ongoing monitoring for safety and performance.

Training should extend beyond standard clinical education to include formal instruction in AI oversight, beginning during residency, followed by supervised senior practice and ultimately formal certification in AI-supervised clinical care.

Medical education should emphasize responsible AI use, awareness of limitations, avoidance of overreliance, and the ethical implications of AI-assisted clinical decision making, including transparency, accountability, bias, and patient trust.
In tier 2, physicians must learn to interpret AI outputs, recognize algorithmic bias, and avoid overreliance.

Medical education must integrate AI fundamentals: data analytics, model validation, and ethics, preparing physicians to use AI tools effectively while integrating them safely and responsibly into clinical practice.
Given rapid AI evolution, continuous education is essential.
As AI assumes routine tasks, medical education must strengthen competencies that remain uniquely human.

unlisted_practices: Medical schools and residency programs should offer structured training in AI and software development for interested trainees.
Ensure physician-developed AI tools operate within institutional governance frameworks.

Define operational boundaries for AI-dominated workflows, including scope of delegated tasks, predefined exclusion criteria for complex cases, escalation pathways for physician review, and continuous performance monitoring with defined audit intervals.

Autonomous AI systems must operate within strictly defined clinical domains with predefined performance thresholds, continuous auditing, and clear assignment of clinical and legal responsibility to supervising physicians or institutions.
Scale AI governance stringency in proportion to the degree of autonomy delegated to AI systems.
Include AI content in licensing and board examinations.
Maintain independent physician practice competence as a safeguard when AI fails.
Ensure robust evaluation of AI tools against clinically meaningful outcomes before use.

screen.reason: This is a framework/perspective paper proposing a five-tier model for integrating AI into clinical practice and medical oncology education.
